newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish yields fall, track foreign markets.
newsitem.headline: Swedish yields fall, track foreign markets.

text.p: Swedish bond yields fell in line with stronger foreign markets at midday on Wednesday and the crown strengthened against the mark, dealers said.
They said that a bond auction in the U.S. and hopes of a balanced U.S. budget triggered the downward movement.
"The crown firmed on commercial flows from Swedish companies and on a generally weaker mark," one dealer said.

The market is waiting for French opinion polls to get a hint of the outcome of the elections to be held on May 25 and June 1 and was also eyeing forecasts from the EU on member states' economic performance under the Maastricht criteria.
"I don't think the forecast will lead to convergence trade even if it turns out to be positive," one dealer said.
He said that the prospect of the French election was weighing on the market too much.
The six month T-bill rate was two basis points lower at 4.17 percent and the 10-year bond fell five bp to 7.28 percent.
The crown firmed to 4.4675 crowns to the mark versus 4,4840 crowns on Tuesday.
